patch.value: Split from PR 24 by orchestrator decision. Own all journaled recovery, native close ownership proof and multi-item compensation. Current PR only performs fresh native close and refuses replay without automatic repair.

Canonicalize short IDs through host native get before every history read, including service-capable contexts; capture history heads before authoritative decision documents and recheck under the same native writer lock; identify own forward close and every restore by a durable unique compensation_id and exact SDK journal identity, never author, message markers or document equality; refuse unrelated same-author native closes and copied transaction markers; native close owns dependent unblock, blocker-field removal, Plan behavior and unchanged warnings, and actual read-back defines successors; persist full immutable member/pre-close bytes digest/post-close history domain before restore, fsync intent, progress and parent-directory updates; durable per-member restored/pending receipts recover own progress without mistaking it for peers; never restore peers or foreign records, and release/claim/restore ABA must be detected from locked native history heads even when all bytes and tokens match; real-process SIGKILL after every forward and reverse step including 0..N member restores with 1-3 dependents converges to exact pre-close item bytes with append-only audit history, no duplicates or loss; peer edits between restores stop with typed partial receipts preserving restored and pending members; lost native returns and ordinary coordinator failures preserve all lifecycle members coherently; packed npm/Bun, non-Git and installed separate/shared SDK layouts exercise every boundary; property tests, revert proofs, full 100 percent coverage, documentation and release gates.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Repository issue https://github.com/unbraind/pm-swarm/issues/34 owns the full rounds 5-15 close protocol. It is related to pm-swarm-y972; the existing dependent-progress issue 32 is linked as a narrower subtask. Removed prototype and tests remain reproducible from commit 0157465. Current PR intentionally has no swarm close transaction, automatic primary restore, member compensation, native-history ownership reconstruction or saved-result adoption.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Scope boundary implemented in PR 24: fresh native close only, immutable refusal after lost returns, prior native closes or legacy markers. Current regressions preserve an unrelated same-author close, service-context short IDs, reopened preimages and native dependent effects after SIGKILL. Full journaled recovery, exact compensation ownership and all multi-member restore progress remain this open Feature and issue 34. No automatic restore implementation ships.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Read the complete linked issues and current implementation. Verify the existing handoff successor guard with real processes; implement native-history-bound durable close intent and per-member recovery through the pinned SDK, with crash and peer-interleaving regressions. value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Native close still owns dependent selection, Plan policy, blocker cleanup and warning tokens. The protocol records a unique SDK-validated compensation identity in native-field intent and derives native episode identities from exact phase/member targets. It compensates interrupted forward prefixes rather than replaying close on a terminal primary. Dependents restore first, with certified lost-progress recovery; final primary restore locks restored dependents while checking the domain. Complete-byte restoration retains all native audit events. README, ARCHITECTURE and native-close documentation describe the state machine.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Storage/lease-tail fault enumeration passed 156/156 checks, including 130 observed-operation injections. A failed final lease cleanup exposed a replay deadlock behind its still-live pin; completed native receipts now replay read-only before lease acquisition. Expanded crash diagnostics include native intent, journal and restore commits before fsync/return, plus durable boundaries. Packed npm/Bun crash coverage is isolated from command smoke tests and removes only its verified synthetic completed members between cases to bound corpus cost; the first growing-fixture packed attempt timed out and is not acceptance evidence.

patch.value: Durable native close recovery on one shared tracker: registered field intent, immutable member restore targets, native phase receipts, guarded success metadata cleanup, and idempotent reverse compensation. Pending recovery precedes terminal and owner guards; unowned or superseded state is preserved. Verification and orchestrator closure remain separate.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Behavioral reverts in disposable copies: original completeClaim produced 45 failing regressions out of 46 (the independent missing-restore guard is separately tested); reverting final handoff cleanup failed 2/2 process scenarios; disabling member resume failed 3/3; weakening ownership history proof failed 3/3; removing final dependency locks failed its real-peer test; removing intent validation failed its persisted-intent test. Restored implementation passed 24/24 focused tests. Additional missing-receipt, Plan and fsync revert controls are running. Isolated packed npm/Bun consumers passed 2/2 acceptance tests, covering 24 real SIGKILL cases. Native Plan closure also matches an independently cloned native SDK oracle.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Pre-gate adversarial review found a real ownership gap: copying the global close episode onto an untouched admitted member could make a peer edit look like an owned forward mutation. A new real-process regression failed before the correction. The native admission hook now signs each exact target, operation, before-head and before/after document hashes under its native item lock, using an ephemeral Ed25519 key. The public key is anchored in registered intent; signed proposals are durably staged by the same host SDK in audited workspace settings before the item write, then frozen into native item history before compensation. The private key is never serialized. Copied episodes and same-author native closes now lack the required signed proposal and are preserved with typed partial receipts. The corrected regression passes; fresh signed-protocol focused tests passed 11/11. Earlier gates and revert proofs are interim evidence and will be refreshed for this design.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The signed-proposal design is now exercised through the pinned pm runner: its eight linked real-tracker regressions passed with the updated timeout. Exact signed proposals also bind unlogged bytes and native SDK history; a copied episode on an untouched member no longer authorizes rollback. Pending compensation validates its complete frozen post-close heads before any restore. Current signature, history-outage, Plan-policy and privacy checks are being measured before the full npm/Bun gates; no claim of final coverage or CI is made yet.

value.author: codex-sol

Restored implementation passed 9 selected critical tests. A native dependent-policy warning also reproduced a compensation admission failure; compensation now drops uncommitted success warnings instead of re-emitting rejected content. Its real-SDK regression passes and an isolated function revert is being verified. Starting unchanged-threshold npm and Bun release gates with fresh home and no global Git identity; earlier aggregate coverage and packed runs remain interim evidence.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: PR 65 is open and queued for CodeRabbit. The first fresh-home full gate passed identity, typecheck, lint, duplication, build and docstrings, then was deliberately stopped during the crash matrix because repeated subprocess V8 collection made each crash case take roughly a minute. That interrupted run is not acceptance evidence. The crash helper now omits V8 output in SIGKILL workers and their retries; every process, boundary and assertion still runs. In-process real-SDK controls measure all authored recovery code; the source inventory and 100/100/100/100 thresholds are unchanged and the full gate will be rerun. Warning-admission revert proof also completed: isolated removal fails; restored code passes.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The remaining crash-matrix cost came from reopening native history for every projected version. Inspection now uses the public SDK replayHistoryToTarget plus replayToCanonicalItemDocument with the native schema on the same verified captured stream. No package projection or predicted lifecycle document is introduced. Normal worker V8 collection is restored; source coverage and every subprocess are measured in the final gate. Timeout headroom is increased for complete real-process matrices under shared-host coverage, without removing any case. Two interrupted collector runs remain excluded from acceptance. Focused native-history and peer-preservation controls are being refreshed before the final npm/Bun gates.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: Focused SDK projection/recovery validation passed 40/40, including one-to-three dependent lost returns and restore progress, process handoff/reclaim, legacy checkpoints, malformed intents, exact signatures, fsync failures, and native warning compensation. value.author: codex-sol
value.text: CodeRabbit round one completed on 1adcdd7 with four inline findings and two documentation findings. New real-SDK regressions reproduced reopened committed work, malformed onPrepared refusals, unrelated fsync coupling, and Windows file-handle policy (4/4 failed before changes). A further failing regression exposed compensation restoring an older intent field; discovery now follows the newest non-restore intent in native history so the newer compensation receipt remains replayable. Typed preparation refusals preserve public portable diagnostics and sanitize ordinary errors. Windows file flushes use writable handles; documentation explicitly separates process-crash recovery from unavailable POSIX directory barriers and power-loss claims. Domain reads authenticate proposals once, and compensation visits affected members only. I am checking the native SDK dependency index as a shared conservative candidate selector, rather than copying lifecycle policy. The interrupted pre-review full gate is not acceptance evidence.

value.author: codex-sol
value.text: The independent copied-phase attack reproduced a genuine result-authentication gap: after SIGKILL immediately after the primary native commit, a peer could publish a copied committed phase with invented warnings and obtain false success while the dependent stayed blocked. The new process regression failed before correction. The original fresh invocation now signs the full terminal result, including all post-heads, proposals and warnings; replay and generation retirement verify that signature against the immutable initial public key. New result/review controls pass 9/9. Packed npm and Bun consumers passed 2/2, covering 24 real SIGKILL cases on the declared SDK floor. Current first-push CI failures were a stale native notification assertion and two missing coverage paths; those are addressed and final full gates remain pending.
